newsitem.title: USA: Omnicom BBDO ends pursuit of Delta account.
newsitem.headline: Omnicom BBDO ends pursuit of Delta account.

text.p: Omnicom's BBDO advertising agency said it has dropped out of the chase for the $90 million Delta Air Lines Inc ad account, ending 51 years of association with the Atlanta-based airline agency.
The remaining finalists for the much-sought airline account are Interpublic's Ammirati Puris Lintas, WPP Plc's Ogilvy & Mather and Cordiant Plc's Saatchi & Saatchi.

Delta put the account into review last December, making BBDO compete in a creative shootout if it wanted to remain on the account. While it ended up among a recent list of finalists, the agency dropped out of the running Thursday, saying it was "not being considered objectively."
Delta could not be reached for immediate comment.

Delta's account went into review not long after Leo Burnett lost its decades-long relationship with UAL Corp's United, marking a particularly turbulent period for ad agencies and the airline business, despite a recent recovery at the big carriers in traffic and profits.

Trade sources have given Ogilvy & Mather the edge in the new Delta review, but BBDO said this was not connected to its decision to exit the competition. Instead, it cited onerous ground rules that kept it from showing its best creative work and said the review had "written BBDO off as a contender."

Phil Dusenberry, chairman of the agency, said, "It had become apparent that we were not being considered objectively or with an open mind and that our particular strengths in creativity were not going to be appreciated in this review."
